surface_forms: la glorieuse soeur de l'impératrice Élisabeth

appraisal_events.evidence: le bruit se répandit que M. de Charlus avait été mis à la porte de chez les Verdurin au moment où il cherchait à violer un jeune musicien... personne dans le petit clan ne voulût plus saluer le baron
appraisal_events.explanation: A degrading rumor about the evening hardens into social fact: former acquaintances of the little clan now decline to greet Charlus, marking his fall from the group.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Vous n'avez pas l'air bien, mon cher cousin... Appuyez-vous sur mon bras. Soyez sûr qu'il vous soutiendra toujours »... c'est ainsi, emmenant à son bras le baron... que sortit la glorieuse soeur de l'impératrice Élisabeth
appraisal_events.explanation: The Queen of Naples publicly takes Charlus's side and his arm, invoking his rank and past courage before the assembled company, visibly restoring his standing at the moment of his humiliation.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Très bien », dit la Reine en continuant si naturellement à parler à M. de Charlus, et d'un air si parfaitement absent que Mme Verdurin douta si c'était à elle que s'adressait ce «très bien»... et sans s'être laissé présenter Morel
appraisal_events.explanation: The Queen barely acknowledges Mme Verdurin's self-introduction and pointedly departs without allowing the presentation of Morel that Mme Verdurin had arranged, a public cut delivered inside Mme Verdurin's own salon.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Mais aussi pourquoi a-t-il joué, c'est idiot »... « il y a longtemps que nous savons qu'il est idiot »... yet M. et Mme Verdurin secretly resolve to fund a hidden pension so that Saniette « ne s'aperçoive pas trop de sa ruine »
appraisal_events.explanation: Saniette's financial ruin and stroke are met with open contempt from the Verdurins, who call him an idiot, even as they privately arrange to support him — a diminishing judgment paired with concealed generosity.

status_effects.explanation: Cut by the little clan and the subject of a degrading rumor, Charlus's local standing collapses.
Charlus is shown crossing out of the petit clan's boundary: fidèles who once deferred to him now decline to greet him.
In a separate, later moment, the Queen's public alliance visibly restores Charlus's standing before the same room that had just humiliated him.
Snubbed by a queen in front of her own salon, her bid for royal recognition is visibly rebuffed.
Morel is barred at the threshold of the presentation he sought: the Queen departs without letting him be introduced.
Saniette is openly called an idiot and his ruin is recounted with a mix of pity and contempt.
The narrator's discovery of Verdurin's secret generosity toward Saniette reveals an unsuspected virtue, though the narrator explicitly stops short of calling him sympathetic.

ambiguities: The Queen's distracted 'très bien' is flagged by the text itself as uncertain in address ('Mme Verdurin douta si c'était à elle que s'adressait ce «très bien»'), so its status as a deliberate snub of Mme Verdurin rather than mere absentmindedness is not fully settled.
